text:
maria: quick dump from last-night's regionals perf run. posting profiler + a config we tried. TL;DR: reduced cross-region spill by ~35% but saw ~8-12ms p50 increase in the zone that lost capacity. need ideas on token-budget shaping and kernel fallback. :thinking:

simon: can you paste the perf numbers and the config you used?

maria: attaching the important bits below (sorry for the wall).

maria: ```
# experiment: interzone soft-steer + aggressive local token_goal
queue_policy:
  mode: soft_steer
  local_fill_threshold: 0.85  # prefer forming local batches until 85%
  cross_zone_steer_after_ms: 30
  max_cross_tokens_per_window: 150000
  per_zone_token_goal: 75000
kv_cache:
  prefetch_enabled: true
  prefetch_ttl_ms: 60000
kernel_selection:
  fallback_sequence_len: 256
  prefer_fp16_if_seq_lt: 256
  prefer_int8_if_seq_ge: 256
  continuous_batching:
    enable_adaptive_shape: true
    target_batch_fill: 0.9
```

anika: nice, a few quick thoughts: 1) soft_steer_after 30ms is aggressive for small QPS zones — they forward too early and you lose KV locality. bump to 75-100ms for zones < 50qps. 2) target_batch_fill 0.9 is optimistic; for mixed seq lengths it causes head-of-line waits. try 0.8 and add leader-timeout = 40ms.

jorge: agreed on the KV locality hit. saw KV miss rate +16% on nodes that received spill. when requests hop, KV cache warms slowly -> thrash. we should add a small per-request metadata field to indicate recent cache_hotset so receiving node can do a lightweight warmup: `X-RW-kv-warm: prefer` (internal only).

devon: also kernel side: if we route more cross-zone, average sequence length changed (shorter tails). we should bias kernel selection to lower-latency fp16 kernels for seq<128, not 256 — that reduced token p99 in my microbench. fallback to int8 for long sequences only when local batch size < 8.

simon: can we have a quick AB plan? i suggest:
- canary eu-west-1 with: cross_zone_steer_after_ms=100, target_batch_fill=0.8, prefer_fp16_if_seq_lt=128
- metrics: p50/p95/p99 tokens latency per-zone, KV miss rate, cross-zone traffic bytes, and cost delta
- run 3h during low traffic then 6h at peak window

maria: sounds good. I'll schedule a canary. need someone to own the harness and the rollback alert. @simon ok for owner?

simon: I can own runs + alert thresholds. please add a synthetic probe for a small chat flow (avg seq 32) and a long completion (avg seq 512).

deploy-bot: scheduled canary: canary-2001234567-euw1 at 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z by maria (3h)

anika: one more thing — add a debug flag to log when requests are steered cross-zone: `X-RW-steer-reason` with values `age|capacity|fallback` so we can correlate reasons with KV-miss spikes.

maria: done. I'll also add a tiny sampler to capture KV keys of steered requests for 1% of traffic (PII-safe).

jorge: if we see KV warmup cost blow up, suggest we implement short-lived sticky sessions for hot keys (70-90s) rather than continuous steering. cheaper than re-warming cache frequently.

devon: if sticky sessions used, update kernel selector to prefer kernels that are more tolerant to batch shape variance (we have a candidate that gives ~3% perf hit but reduces tail variance).

simon: ok runbook: rollback when per-zone p95 increases >20% or cross-zone bytes increase >50% vs baseline. otherwise escalate to runtime oncall.

maria: thanks all — I'll post results + profiler links in this thread after the canary. :rocket: :eyes:
